data.description:
# Surface repeated non-fatal LLM step failures in gate run summaries

Split out of bug `tasty-unappeased-leopard` (b273-e0ba-f719-4f1c) at operator direction;
that ticket now covers only the build-drift warning.

## Problem

During a `review-plan` run, the overlap judge failed on EVERY batch:

    llm call [overlap-judge] mode=single_turn FAILED in 310.0s: Exceeded maximum output retries (2)
    overlap judge batch call failed; treating as abstain

Three batches were observed, each ~310s, each ending in `abstain`. The failures are
non-fatal by design (an abstaining sub-step must not fail a review), so they never reach
the verdict — the run paid ~15 minutes of wall time for a step that contributed nothing
and reported nothing a caller would notice. The only trace was interleaved log lines.

## What is wanted

A gate run summary (the verdict payload / JSON output a caller consumes) should carry a
count of non-fatal LLM step failures, so repeated silent degradation is visible without
scraping logs. Scope, shape, and whether this is per-step or aggregate are open design
questions for whoever picks this up.

## Notes

- Must remain non-fatal: this is reporting, not a new failure mode.
- Related: `7fa8102477` ("Bound malformed overlap judge calls") reduced the latency cost
  of the specific overlap-judge failure, but not the invisibility of the class.
data.title: Surface repeated non-fatal LLM step failures in gate run summaries
